inspiration.observed_pattern: MariaDB JSON_ARRAYAGG accepts an aggregate-local LIMIT so only a bounded number of values are serialized from the input relation.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored batch manifest report. Each batch serializes its two highest-priority item labels with JSON_ARRAYAGG ORDER BY and LIMIT while COUNT records the full batch size; the source tables, storage engine, identifiers, and regression setup are new.

fixture_notes: Batch 21 has three items ranked 90, 80, and 70, so only the first two labels are serialized while item_count remains 3. Batch 22 has two items and both are serialized. Priority and item ID provide stable aggregate ordering.
determinism_notes: Batch IDs, item IDs, labels, priorities, aggregate ordering, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE batch_items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_id INT NOT NULL, item_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, priority INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT batch_id, JSON_ARRAYAGG(item_label ORDER BY priority DESC, item_id ASC LIMIT 2) AS top_items, COUNT(*) AS item_count FROM batch_items GROUP BY batch_id ORDER BY batch_id
